rows.source: FillInput(): state = 0x853c49e6748fea9b, next() = u32(state = state*6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407 >> 33); words[0] = FloatEdges[tid%12]; words[1] = FloatEdges[(tid/12+tid)%12]; a = tid<16 ? IntegerEdges[tid%8] : next()<<32 | next(); b = tid<16 ? IntegerEdges[(tid/8+tid*3)%8] : (tid%5==0 ? a : next()<<32 | next()); words[2..5] = a lo, a hi, b lo, b hi; words[6] = 0xabcd0000 | HalfEdges[tid%12]; words[7] = 0x12340000 | HalfEdges[(tid/12+tid*5)%12]. The operand order of next()<<32 | next() is unspecified in C++; the literal table is from a g++ build (the compiler that builds the tests).

notes: The test loads 8 dwords per lane: f32 a,b -> v4,v5; u64 a -> v[6:7]; u64 b -> v[8:9]; f16 a,b (with 0xabcd/0x1234 high halves) -> v14,v15. Each compare block reads only one of these groups, and each writes its own bit of v10/v11 (v_lshl_or_b32 vX, v20, bit, vX), so the same words are replayed three times with three row mappings and each part compares only the bits of its group (column_masks: compare (oracle & mask) with (host & mask)).
EXEC: every v_cmpx block saves exec_lo in s30 and restores it (s_mov_b32 exec_lo, s30) before the next block; the body ends with full EXEC.
Accumulators v10, v11 start at 0 (pre, as the prologue).

Part 2 (64-bit integer compares): rows = Input words 2..5 (a lo, a hi, b lo, b hi); pre moves them into v[6:7] and v[8:9] (v6,v7 -> v8,v9 first, then v4,v5 -> v6,v7). Asserted bits: v10 bits 8..31 (compares 8..31), v11 bit 0 (32), v11 bits 19,20 (51, 52).
verified: disassembly: llvm-mc gfx1030 (gfx1013 cross-check for opcode aliasing) of the word range; Run()/Check() read for register use, row layout and asserted columns; block boundaries and per-block input registers extracted from the disassembly
